summary: Attempt 2 discharges O-002 to O-013 on top of the committed attempt-1 build. ScanStore gained public ChargedSize/ChargedOnDisk, and every scan in the tests asserts that their sums equal Totals. SizeProbe now has a third case: files listed at 64 MiB or more, backed by a documentary open-file test and a counting test for a file that is held open and still growing. DFS reparse points are classified as links. The long-path case now also probes a WOF file and a hardlink pair under a path over 400 characters with trailing-dot names. The window gained a fourth ending (Scan failed), a used-space coverage line on drive-root scans, and repair of the trailing quote Windows leaves on a quoted path argument. eng/dotnet.ps1 now pins SDK 10.0.401 and runs the installer only when its Authenticode signature is valid and Microsoft's. The architecture rules, including the widened and new ones, are enforced by ArchitectureRulesTests. The as-built design amendments are in docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md. All 86 tests pass. A real C:\ scan through the app with the argument quoted as "C:\" finished in 71.1 s and reported 736.9 GB in use with 50.7 GB not seen.

files.why: O-002: public ChargedSize(i) and ChargedOnDisk(i) return 0 for Link and HardlinkDuplicate entries, and Size/OnDisk otherwise. Doc comments say to sum these and never Size() or OnDisk().

O-004: LargeFileThreshold (64 MiB) and IsDue(): probe when the file is a WOF suspect, or its listed EndOfFile or AllocationSize is at least 64 MiB. Never for cloud-only files. The class doc now names three cases.
O-004: a newly charged file is probed when SizeProbe.IsDue says so. The first-repeat probe still skips records that are already probed.
O-005: IO_REPARSE_TAG_DFS (0x8000000A) is a Link, so a scan never continues onto another server's volume.
O-005: IO_REPARSE_TAG_DFS constant.
O-005: the Link doc names the DFS tag.
O-009: CommandLine.RootArgument turns a single trailing '"' (left by Windows argv escaping of "C:\") back into '\'. Pure and public, so the App can use it and the tests can table it.
O-009: passes the argument through CommandLine.RootArgument.

O-008: any non-ArgumentException from the scan leads to a 'Scan failed' ending with the exception type and message, and the pickers are re-enabled. O-013: on drive-root scans, Finished and Stopped show the volume's used space (DriveInfo TotalSize − TotalFreeSpace, read on the scan thread) and the bytes the scan did not see.
The comment names the fourth ending.

O-011: installs pinned SDK 10.0.401 with -Version, not -Channel 10.0. The downloaded dotnet-install.ps1 runs only if Get-AuthenticodeSignature reports Valid with an O=Microsoft Corporation signer; otherwise it is deleted and the script exits 1.
O-002: AssertChargedBytesAreTheTotals (sums over entries 1..Count-1 equal Totals.Bytes and BytesOnDisk). Scans.Run applies it to every scan it runs.
O-002: the charged-sum assertion on the partial store of a scan cancelled mid-way (this test calls Scanner.Scan directly).
O-002: the charged-sum assertion on the bare-drive listing (this test also calls Scanner.Scan directly).

O-002: ChargedSize is 64 MiB for the charged name and 0 (size and on disk) for every duplicate. The Probes comment explains that the large-file rule, not the repeat, probes when the current name is seen first.
O-002: every link has ChargedSize and ChargedOnDisk of 0.

O-004: documentary TheListingOfAFileHeldOpenIsCurrentOnceTheWriterFlushes, and counting ALargeFileHeldOpenAndGrowingIsChargedAtItsTrueSize (128 MiB while open, SizeProbed). Case 7's 64 MiB sparse file now meets the large rule and is asserted as probed, with the probe equal to the listing. Case 8's all-hole file shrinks to 16 MiB so the sparse guard is what decides.

O-003: a WOF file 'wof.' and a hardlink pair 'a.'/'b.' under a >400-character path in a trailing-dot folder 'probe.'. Asserts SizeProbed on both probed records, ProbeFailed on neither, Probes 2 and ProbeFailures 0.
O-005: a DFS (0x8000000A) directory row is classified as Link.

O-010: the symlink helpers turn error 1314 into a failure saying Developer Mode is off or blocked by policy. There is no fallback and nothing is skipped. Write(FileStream, long) is made public for the open-file tests.
O-009: a table test of the argument mapping (quoted drive root, folder with a space, share, and unquoted paths left alone).

O-003, O-006, O-007: the architecture rules checked over the source tree. The four original rules; the reparse rule widened to src/** (except EntryClassifier.cs and Kernel32.cs) with 0x0*400\b; Explicit=true and SkipException added to the never-skipped rule; and the new rule confining interop to Native/** plus TestNative.cs.

O-012 plus the key decisions O-004, O-005 and O-013 ask for. The as-built amendments to the components, contracts, key decisions and architecture rules, so no later slice 'corrects' the code back to the stale design text.

obligations.how: Added public ScanStore.ChargedSize(i) and ChargedOnDisk(i), which return 0 for Link and HardlinkDuplicate entries and are documented as the accessors to sum. Scans.Run asserts after every scan that their sums over entries 1..Count-1 equal Totals.Bytes/BytesOnDisk, and the two tests that call Scanner.Scan directly (mid-scan cancel, bare drive) assert it explicitly. That covers every counting-rule test. The hardlink and link tests also assert 0 per duplicate and per link. On the real C: scan the sums equalled Totals. As decided, the display accessor that follows a duplicate to its charged record is left to the tree slice.

Built as decided. C-004 (LongPathTests.ReachesPathsWin32WouldAlter) now puts a WOF file 'wof.' and a hardlink pair 'a.'/'b.' in a trailing-dot folder under a path over 400 characters, and asserts SizeProbed with no ProbeFailed on both probed records (Probes 2, ProbeFailures 0). The interop rule ((Library|Dll)Import only under src/FsAnalyser.Core/Native/** and tests/.../TestNative.cs) is enforced by ArchitectureRulesTests.InteropLivesOnlyInNative. The Win32Path type and GetNativePath wait for a third Win32 caller, as decided. The fix text's Path.GetFullPath rule was not added, because the decision took only the interop rule. On the finding's '3 unexplained probe failures': the C: re-measure lists all 7 current failures with their errors (32 on pagefile.sys and hiberfil.sys; 5 on a GoogleUpdater crx_cache file, Windows\Panther\setupact.log and a WinSxS .xsd; 363 'cloud file metadata is corrupt' on two cloud-tagged leftovers in another project's %TEMP%\fsa-guard-tests). None is a path-form error such as 3 or 123.

I added the documentary test first, as decided: OnDiskSizeTests.TheListingOfAFileHeldOpenIsCurrentOnceTheWriterFlushes. It measured that after Flush(true) the listing matches FILE_STANDARD_INFO while the file is still open (64 MiB; the throwaway run saw 76,677,120 allocated on both). Without a flush the listing lagged (1 MiB listed against 64 MiB real) and had caught up within 2 s. That window is timing-dependent, so it is documented and not asserted. Option (a) is built: SizeProbe.IsDue also probes non-cloud files listed at 64 MiB or more, never twice. ALargeFileHeldOpenAndGrowingIsChargedAtItsTrueSize proves that a file held open and still growing is charged at 128 MiB. The key decision now reads 'three cases' in docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md. On real C: (WSL was not running, and I did not start it) the rule probed 964 files of 64 MiB or more, 0 of which disagreed with their listing. The scan took 61.7 s warm.
EntryClassifier treats IO_REPARSE_TAG_DFS (0x8000000A) as a Link alongside 0xA0000003 and 0xA000000C, so the scan never enters it. EntryClassifierTests has a DFS row (22 rows pass).

ArchitectureRulesTests.OnlyTheClassifierReadsTheReparseAttribute scans src/**/*.cs and *.xaml, except EntryClassifier.cs and Native/Kernel32.cs, for FileAttributes.ReparsePoint, FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT, IsReparsePoint and 0x0*400\b. It passes on the tree. A planted '0x400' in MainWindow.xaml.cs made it fail, and the plant was removed. The widened rule is also recorded in docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md. The engine's declared rule list lives in the design record, which this stage cannot edit.

ArchitectureRulesTests.CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped adds \bExplicit\s*=\s*true and SkipException to the three original patterns over tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/**. SkipException is written as Skip(?:Exception) so the rule file does not match itself. A planted '[Fact(Explicit = true)]' made it fail, and the plant was removed. As decided, --fail-skips waits for a move to xUnit v3; the build is on 2.9.3.

MainWindow now catches any non-ArgumentException from the scan task and shows a fourth 'Scan failed: <path>' ending with the exception type and message. The existing finally block stops the timer and re-enables the pickers. Exercised by a temporary injected InvalidOperationException, reverted and rebuilt afterwards. UI Automation read 'Scan failed: C:\inject-scan-failure', 'InvalidOperationException: injected for a smoke test', process alive, 'Choose a folder...' enabled=True.

Added public Core helper CommandLine.RootArgument (a single trailing '"' becomes '\'), called from App.OnStartup, with the CommandLineTests table (6 rows pass). The app launched with the argument quoted as "C:\", the exact form that failed in attempt 1, now reaches 'Finished: C:\'.

TempTree.DirectorySymlink and FileSymlink go through CreateSymlink. It catches HResult error 1314 and throws saying Windows refused the link because Developer Mode is off or blocked by policy, and that the link tests need it and are not skipped. No CreateSymbolicLinkW fallback exists (none was ever written), and the design text naming it is replaced in docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md.

eng/dotnet.ps1 now passes -Version 10.0.401 instead of -Channel 10.0. It runs the downloaded dotnet-install.ps1 only when Get-AuthenticodeSignature reports Valid with an O=Microsoft Corporation signer; otherwise it deletes the file and exits 1. global.json is unchanged. End to end: a scratch copy of the script in %TEMP% with no .dotnet downloaded the installer, found it Valid (CN=Microsoft Corporation, issuer Microsoft Code Signing PCA 2024), installed 10.0.401 and printed 10.0.401 (exit 0). A tampered copy of the installer reads NotSigned and the same check rejects it. The scratch copy was deleted.

docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md amends the design to match the code, O-001 and the recorded deviations. It covers the custom open-addressing FileId index (not a HashSet), ServerGarbageCollection, the SDDL raw-mask 0x100080 deny ACE, the flushed sparse fixture, totals excluding the root, CloudOnly on files only, public ScanResult.Root, the m2 note (ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND on the first call is an empty listing) and the m9 text. It also carries this attempt's decisions: three probe cases, DFS as a link, the coverage-gap deferral, the new and widened architecture rules, and the pinned and verified bootstrap. Limit: the engine's own stored design record (design-slice-1.json in the DB) cannot be edited from this stage. The repo document says it supersedes that record, and the deviations here repeat the amendments.

On a drive-root scan (root of the form X:\), the scan thread reads DriveInfo TotalSize − TotalFreeSpace. Finished then shows 'The volume reports <used> in use, so <gap> of it was not seen by this scan (file-system metadata, folders it could not read, and anything else an ordinary account cannot list)'. Stopped shows the gap as 'not in this partial scan'. A key decision in docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md leaves explaining the gap (metafiles, the unreadable-folder breakdown, the coverage panel) to the architecture's later coverage-panel slice. Measured through the app on C:: 736.9 GB in use, 686.1 GB seen on disk, 50.7 GB not seen. I did not request the read-denied-folders operation, because nothing in this slice's gate needs its number.

Throwaway full Scanner.Scan of C:\ with the new code, deleted afterwards. WSL was not running and I did not start it. Completed in 61.7 s warm: 4,118,424 entries, 259,041 probes, 7 probe failures, 599 unreadable folders. Charged sums equal Totals. 964 probed files of 64 MiB or more, 0 disagreeing with a fresh listing. The failures and their errors are listed under O-003.
Final full run: Total 86, Passed 86, none skipped. %TEMP%\fsa-tests left with 0 entries.

The argument form that failed in attempt 1 now scans the whole drive. 'Finished: C:\', 3,435,933 files and 665,616 folders, 16,864 links not followed, 952.5 GB in files taking 686.1 GB on disk. 'The volume reports 736.9 GB in use, so 50.7 GB of it was not seen by this scan (...)'. Read in 71.1 s, 7 probe-failure note, 599 unreadable folders. Peak paged 584 MiB.

Process alive, 'Choose a folder...' enabled=True. The file was reverted (content equal to the pre-injection text, 0 occurrences of the injection) and the App rebuilt with 0 errors.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests --filter "FullyQualifiedName~FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.<each filter>"
tests.note: All 13 case commands in `cases` plus the new filters (both open-file tests, CommandLineTests 6, ArchitectureRulesTests 5, EntryClassifierTests 22, and the budget test) were run one by one. Each exited 0 with Passed >= 1 and Failed 0.

deviations: O-004's premise did not hold as stated. The documentary test the decision asked for (hold the file open, grow it to 64 MiB, Flush(true), compare) measured the listing as current, not stale. The only lag seen was between an unflushed write and the lazy writer (1 MiB listed against 64 MiB real, gone within 2 s), which is timing-dependent and is documented, not asserted. The decision to take option (a) regardless is built as decided. The documentary test asserts the agreement that was actually observed.

Case 7's shape ('4 KiB written in 64 MiB' sparse) now meets the person's 64 MiB large-file rule, so it is probed. Its test asserts SizeProbed with the probe equal to the listing, instead of 'Probes 0'. The listing is still shown to be right for sparse files. Case 8's all-hole sparse file (no size fixed in the case) is 16 MiB, so the sparse guard, not the large rule, is what keeps it unprobed.

Architecture rules: this stage cannot edit the engine's declared rule list, which lives in the design record. The widened and new rules are enforced by tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/ArchitectureRulesTests.cs and recorded in docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md. In that test's source, SkipException is written as Skip(?:Exception) and (LibraryImport|DllImport) as (Library|Dll)Import. They match the same text, and the rule file does not match itself.

The charged-sum assertion is applied in Scans.Run, so every scan made through the helper checks it, plus explicit calls in the two tests that call Scanner.Scan directly. It is not a hand-written line in each test body, which makes a future counting test that forgets it impossible.

O-012's amendments live in the repo (docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md) and not in the engine's stored design, which a builder cannot write. The document states that it supersedes the original design text.
not_built: Path\.GetFullPath-only-in-LongPath.cs architecture rule (in O-003's fix text). The person's decision on M2 took only the interop rule, so it was not added.
The Win32Path type and ScanStore.GetNativePath (O-003). They are deferred by the decision to the slice that adds a third Win32 caller.
A display accessor that follows a hardlink duplicate to its charged record (O-002). It is deferred by the decision to the tree slice.
--fail-skips (O-007). It is deferred by the decision until an actual move to xUnit v3; the project is on 2.9.3.
Counting large-file disagreements 'with WSL running' (O-004 fix text). WSL was not running and I did not start a VM on the owner's machine, so the C: count (964 probed, 0 disagreeing) is without WSL.
follow_ups: A C: scan makes 259,041 probes (about 7.5% of 3.4M files), almost all of them WOF suspects and first hardlink repeats (WinSxS). The large-file rule added only 964. The design's premise that probes are rare does not hold on this PC, although the scan still took 61.7 s warm and 71.1 s through the app. The cold-scan cost of the probes is worth measuring.

The large-file rule makes pagefile.sys and hiberfil.sys fail their probe (error 32, sharing violation) on every C: scan, so the Finished note always counts at least these. Their listing values are correct. A later slice may want to treat a sharing violation on paging files as expected rather than as a probe failure.
%TEMP%\fsa-guard-tests holds cloud-tagged leftover files from another project's tests (error 363 when probed). They are not this repo's and were not touched.

ChargedSize reads HardlinkDuplicate, which the scanner sets just after Append. A reader during a scan (the tree slice) could briefly see a duplicate as charged. Setting the flag before the count is published would close that.
m7 (deferred by the person): CancelSynchronousIo for a network or cloud call that blocks, with 995 handled as cancellation. It still needs a later slice that hardens network and cloud volumes.

O-013's explanation of the coverage gap (NTFS metafiles, a breakdown of the unreadable folders) belongs to the coverage-panel slice. The registered read-denied-folders operation can measure how much of the 50.7 GB the 599 unreadable folders hold.
The engine's stored design for SL-020 still carries the pre-amendment text. The design-slice stage may want to take docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md into its record.
